full_judgment: 3. The rule is being contested by the respondent Nos. 1 and 4 by filing separate affidavits- in-opposition denying material allegations. Their common case is that Wazir Bibi had no Khas possession in the disputed land and she had only rent receiving interest therein after settling the same with tenants, and heirs of Wazir Bibi inherited only rent receiving interest and no notice under section 57(1) of the Bengal Tenancy Act was given to the Collector by Shamsun Nahar Begum and others and they did not take possession of the disputed land. The story of gift is false, concocted and malafide. The petitioners did not acquire title and possession in the disputed land and award of compensation for the requisition and acquisition of the same was not prepared in their names. The land of CS Plot Nos. 677, 680 and 681 was not de-requisitioned. Notice of de-requisition of part of CS Plot No. 680 was issued in the name of Alep Ali and not the petitioners who had no right, title and interest therein. But subsequently entire 32.50 acres of lands were permanently acquired by Gazette Notification dated 4.10.1951 and as such question of de-requisition and delivery of possession of the disputed land to the petitioners does not arise. On the request of the Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, in short, BCSIR, government by letter dated 18.10.1955 decided to transfer 20 acres out of 32.50 acre of acquired land for its regional laboratories at Dhaka and subsequently leased out the same to the BCSIR by deed dated 10.12.1956 and possession of the land was duly delivered to BCSIR. As BCSIR could not accommodate all their constructions within the said 20 acres of land they requested for allotment of further 10 acres of land but the Government allotted 7.60 acres of additional land out of the said acquired land by Memo dated 26.8.1957 and handed over possession of the same to the BCSIR including the disputed land. After allotment and delivery of possession therein BCSIR constructed several buildings in the said land. As the disputed land was not de-requisitioned question of restoration of possession to the petitioners does not arise at all. Report submitted by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka to the Ministry on 10.5.1983 is incorrect and suppression of facts. The petitioners managed to prepare the said report and the map attached thereto in illegal collusion with the staff of Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka. Similarly report dated 29.11.1984 of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka is also biased and incorrect by misrepresentation and suppression of facts. Report dated 20.10.1986 of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) Dhaka is also biased, incorrect and obtained by undue influence and misrepresentation of facts. BCSIR is not in possession of any land beyond the land allotted to it the petitioners are not entitled to restoration of possession in the disputed land which was never de-requisitioned rather permanently acquired and allotted to the BCSIR and in its possession after construction of buildings therein.
